variables.{{keywords}}: Up to six visual keywords extracted from the narration beat.
variables.{{keywordsAll}}: Every significant word extracted from the narration beat, unclipped.
variables.{{subjectType}}: A human-figure or non-human-subject hint inferred from the narration.
variables.{{sentiment}}: The emotional meaning inferred from the complete narration beat.
variables.{{storyBeat}}: The scene's role in the opening, development, turning point, reflection, or resolution.
variables.{{visualAction}}: A concrete action, prop, and environment inferred from the narration.
variables.{{shotPlan}}: A camera and composition plan selected to make the action readable and vary neighboring scenes.
variables.{{castPlan}}: A scene-by-scene choice between a solo woman, solo man, or rare shared two-person turning point.
variables.{{castBrief}}: A compact cast rule for providers that perform better with short prompts.
variables.{{continuity}}: Character-continuity guidance that also forces scene-to-scene visual variety.
variables.{{castTags}}: A short cast tag for tag-format profiles; empty for topics with no recurring cast.
variables.{{topicDirection}}: One sentence of topic-specific direction; empty for topics that impose no cast rules.
variables.{{age}}: Cast age descriptor resolved once from the whole script (topic packs with a cast).
variables.{{ageDetail}}: Supporting age detail for the cast, e.g. clothing and facial cues.

photographic.label: Photographic (retro film, no people)
photographic.sceneTemplate: Photograph the feeling of this narration beat as an empty scene with no people in it. Narration: {{line}}. Story position: {{storyBeat}}. Emotional interpretation: {{sentiment}}. Visual anchors: {{keywords}}. Do not stage the people the line mentions. Translate them into the place and into the one or two objects the line implies, chosen from an unmade bed in morning light, two cups of coffee going cold, a candle burning down, cut roses on a table, a wrapped gift, a balloon drifting against the sky, an open window, or a worn letter. Shoot from far away at sunrise or sunset, looking out through foreground leaves, branches, tall grass, or flowers toward the ocean, a shoreline, a quiet garden, a field, or a still sunlit room. If any figure appears at all, keep it tiny and distant on the horizon, backlit by the low sun into a plain dark silhouette, with no visible face, no visible hands, and no readable detail. {{continuity}} Never repeat the same location and framing across neighboring scenes. Build the vertical frame from layered foreground and background depth and leave calm empty space for captions.
photographic.stylePrompt: Nostalgic film photograph shot on an old grainy 35mm camera and scanned from a faded print: heavy film grain, soft imperfect focus, gentle halation and light leaks, lifted low contrast, dust and slight vignetting. Landscapes, still lifes, and quiet interiors seen from a distance, never a portrait. Sunrise and sunset over the ocean, a horizon glimpsed through trees, plants, and backlit wildflowers, a calm shoreline, a garden at dusk. Romantic domestic objects: balloons, roses, wrapped gifts, coffee cups, candles, an unmade bed by a bright window. Low warm sun, long shadows, amber and rose glow, deep quiet shade. Burnt umber, brick red, rust, ember orange, ochre, muted golden yellow, restrained moss and olive green, deep teal, navy, and near-black. Calm, unhurried, tender melancholy, and a strong sense of memory.
